title: IaC CD: safe rollforward upgrades with preflight linting, policy gates, and post-apply health checks for Private VPCs
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) deployments are sensitive to Terraform plan/apply mistakes during module upgrades. We need a CI/CD workflow that prevents accidental destructive changes, enforces policy-as-code, performs preflight linting, and executes safe rollforward upgrades with automated post-apply health verification and an automated rollback path.

Goal: Implement a reproducible pipeline and guidelines for all Private IaC repos that ensures upgrades are validated via linting and policy gates (Conftest/OPA or equivalent), plan diffs are human-reviewed or auto-approved when non-breaking, canary applies occur in an isolated staging workspace, and post-apply health checks verify networking/service availability before promoting changes to production VPCs.

Scope: Terraform-based modules and overlays used by Private deployments (VPC modules, networking, bastion, peering, routing, KMS integrations). Pipeline touchpoints: pre-commit & pre-push hooks, CI linting, plan-only PR checks, gated apply job with canary workspace, post-apply verification step, and documented recovery steps.

Out of scope: non-Terraform IaC (helm charts, app infra), full replacement of Terraform Cloud or Atlantis—this work should integrate with our existing tooling choices in each repo.
acceptance_criteria: All Private IaC repos have a CI workflow that runs terraform fmt, tflint, tfsec/Checkov, and Conftest/OPA policy checks on PRs
PRs produce a machine-readable plan comment (JSON) and a human-friendly summary; destructive changes are highlighted
Apply step runs only after explicit approval or automated canary pass for non-destructive upgrades
Canary workspace executes apply against an isolated staging VPC with minimal blast radius
Post-apply health checks (network routing, example instance boot, endpoint smoke tests) run and must pass before promotion
Automated rollback plan is created if health checks fail; runbook links included in PR and pipeline UI
Pipeline supports toggling strictness via repo-level config and central policy registry
Documentation and runbook exist in Confluence and link from PR templates
tasks: Draft CI pipeline template (GitHub Actions) with preflight steps: terraform init/validate, terraform fmt -check, tflint, tfsec/Checkov
Define central Rego policies and Conftest tests for our security/ops guardrails (disallowed public subnets, KMS not in allowed key aliases, IAM rules), publish to policy-registry repo
Add plan exporter to produce JSON plan artifacts and a DSL for checking allowed change patterns
Implement canary workspace automation: create ephemeral state workspace, apply with minimal targets, tag resources for easy cleanup
Implement post-apply health checks: VPC reachability tests, routing table verification, test instance SSH/HTTP smoke, KMS key usage smoke
Add auto-rollback job that runs terraform apply -var-file=rollback.tfvars against production in failure case
Create PR template and policy for required reviewers (infra-owner + service-owner) for destructive changes
Document runbook and add alerting hooks to Console dashboards for failed upgrades

implementation_notes: Implementation will favor composable templates. Reuse infra-ci-templates for Actions; provide a small wrapper script 'rw-iac-validate' to normalize outputs across repos. Policy registry will live under repos/policy-registry with versioned tags. Canary applies will be implemented as 'apply --target' with pre-created ephemeral workspaces. Health checks implemented as a small test harness (go + shell) that accepts a plan artifact and executes smoke tests against the target environment. All logs and artifacts stored in build artifacts and linked to PRs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from Conftest/opa blocking safe changes. Mitigation: staged rollout of new rules, maintain allowlist and an exceptions process via a central governance ticket
Risk: Canary workspace not fully representative of production. Mitigation: define a minimal set of resources that must exist in canary and keep a sync job to validate parity
Risk: Rollback may not be idempotent for some DB/network adjustments. Mitigation: require manual approval for changes touching DB or stateful components; add explicit migration steps to PRs
Risk: Increased CI runtime and flakiness. Mitigation: cache modules, parallelize linting and security scans, and set timeouts; surface results incrementally in PRs
